answer: Give every agent a depth in the ocean instead of a free pass. A new agent starts shallow with a refundable deposit locked in a sable ink ledger, and may only take small jobs. Each finished job earns a violet stamp from the client, stamped into a record that cannot be sold or moved. Three stamps from three clients move the agent deeper, where bigger jobs pay more. A fake caught cheating loses its deposit and stamps, and starts shallow again. One fake costs assumed here $2,500, about $2.5 million for 1,000 fakes, so flooding the ocean costs real money, like a diver earning every metre down.
